basics.name: Tristan Lazard
basics.label: PhD in Computational Pathology
basics.summary: After completing my undergraduate studies in biology at ENS Ulm, I pursued and graduated with a Master's degree in Applied Mathematics from UPMC Sorbonne. Subsequently, I earned my PhD from CBIO at Mines ParisTech. My doctoral research bridged the fields of biology, mathematics, and computer science, with a particular focus on developing algorithms to learn representations of large-scale microscopy images (WSIs). My interests broadly span these areas, including biology and evolution, applied mathematics, as well as computer science and machine learning.

work.name: CBIO - Mines-Paristech
work.summary: During my PhD, I focused on training predictive models from Whole Slide Images of cancerous tissues. Besides their clinical use, my goal was to understand these models to improve our understanding of the disease. I also worked on developing unsupervised techniques to train representations of these biological samples. This effort resulted in 5 papers, 1 patent, and a prize-winning solution at an international data challenge, Visiomel.

work.name: CMM, Mines-Paristech
work.summary: In partnership with L’Or´eal, I created an algorithm for automatically counting melanocytes in microscopic images. This solution has been integrated into the processing pipeline and is now utilized in regular research.

work.name: IBPS, Sorbonne University
work.summary: I developped an algorithm for calculating phylogenetic trees from huge genetic sequence data (-omics data).

work.name: Collège de France
work.summary: I worked on a model of random mutualistic network. Most notably studied its asymptotic behaviours and developed an algorithm to infer its parameters from a sampled network.

computing: ML+image processing libs (PyTorch, OpenCV, PIL, Sklearn)
